defendant: LINCOLN ELECTRIC AUTOMATION, INC. (F/K/A WAYNE TRAIL TECHNOLOGIES, INC.), 407 South Main Street, Fort Laramie, OH 45845. An Ohio corporation. Name changed from Wayne Trail Technologies, Inc. by Certificate of Amendment filed with the Ohio Secretary of State on 2020-12-18. No attorney ever appeared.
agreement: Grant Agreement. The complaint calls it a Grant Agreement throughout, with JobsOhio as Grantor and the defendant as Grantee, and pleads that JobsOhio 'agreed to provide Defendant $100,000.00 in grant funds conditioned on Defendant complying with all terms of the Grant Agreement.'
program: Not named. The complaint describes JobsOhio's mission and 'the use of strategic grants and project funding' but never names one of JobsOhio's published incentive programs.
amount_sought: $100,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. This is the full grant amount disbursed.
job_commitments: From paragraph 4: create 50 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $3,750,000.00; retain 170 existing jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $13,000,000.00; and make a total fixed asset investment at the Project Site of $6,800,000.00. Project Site is both 407 South Main Street and 203 East Park Street, Fort Laramie, OH 45845. Metric Evaluation Date 2019-12-31; metrics to be maintained through the Metric Expiration Date of 2021-12-31.
shortfall: From paragraph 10: the defendant's own 2021 Annual Report 'acknowledged that Defendant failed to satisfy its Metric Commitments.' It 'only created 13 new jobs, with an associated payroll of $817,938.21' against a requirement of 50 new jobs and $3,750,000.00 of payroll, and 'further failed to make total fixed asset investments in the amount of $6,800,000.00.' The complaint does not state what fixed asset investment was actually made. JobsOhio issued a demand letter dated 2022-08-10 (Exhibit 3) demanding repayment of the $100,000.00; the defendant 'refused and/or failed to return the grant funds.'
repayment_quote: Section 5, quoted at paragraph 5: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added).' ||| Section 6(b), quoted at paragraph 6: '(b) Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the "Annual Report"). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9. (Emphasis added).' ||| Section 9(b), quoted at paragraph 7: '(b) Remedies. Following a default by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (Emphasis added). (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law.' ||| The complaint also pleads at paragraph 10 (the second paragraph numbered 10) that 'Pursuant to Section 9(e) of the Grant Agreement, Defendant is further liable for JobsOhio's attorney fees, costs, and expenses incurred in bringing this action,' but does not quote Section 9(e).
remedy_named: Repayment. Section 9(b)(ii) is headed 'Demand Repayment of Grant Funds.' The words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear. This differs from the Olive AI Talent Acquisition Services Agreement, whose Section 9(b)(ii) is headed 'Liquidated Damages.' The section numbering, 5 for metrics and 9(b) for remedies, is parallel but not identical.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. Paragraph 4 says the Grant Agreement is 'attached hereto as Exhibit 2.' The complaint PDF is 29 pages: a 4-page complaint followed by Exhibit 1 (the Ohio Secretary of State Certificate of Amendment), Exhibit 2 (the Grant Agreement itself) and Exhibit 3 (the 2022-08-10 demand letter). This is the opposite of the Olive AI case, where JobsOhio refused to attach the agreement on confidentiality and trade-secret grounds. The exhibit pages were retrieved but their full text was not transcribed.
outcome: Dismissed by JobsOhio without prejudice, before any answer was filed. The filing is captioned 'PLAINTIFF JOBSOHIO'S NOTICE OF DISMISSAL WITHOUT PREJUDICE' and reads in full: 'Now comes the Plaintiff JobsOhio ("JobsOhio') and hereby dismisses this case without prejudice.' No judgment was ever entered. The defendant never appeared or answered; JobsOhio filed four consecutive consents to move or plead between 2022-10-20 and 2022-12-21, which is consistent with negotiation, but no settlement agreement, judgment entry or dismissal entry stating terms is in the file.
amount_recovered: Not stated anywhere in the record. No judgment was entered, no satisfaction of judgment was filed, and the dismissal notice states no terms. Nothing in the file establishes that JobsOhio received any money.

notes: This is the clearest public statement of a JobsOhio cash grant agreement's repayment terms found in this batch, and unlike the Olive AI case the agreement itself is attached to the complaint. Counsel is the same firm as in the Olive AI suit, Mann & Carducci Co. LPA (Robert J. Mann, Mary Spahia-Carducci). Note the mismatch with the grant schedule: the input file records $1,000,000 paid to The Lincoln Electric Company across 2017 and 2023, while this suit concerns a single $100,000 grant to Wayne Trail Technologies, which Lincoln Electric later renamed. The complaint has two paragraphs numbered 10, an error in the original. The complaint does not say what fixed asset investment the company actually made, only that it fell short of $6,800,000.00, and it says nothing about the 170 retained jobs.
